tiers.label: canonical substantive authorities with reliable identity/text
tiers.caution: `decided` and `decided_brief` are sample-derived upper bounds on authority; they are not legal weight.

tiers.label: verified legal objects
tiers.caution: Population needs document_enrichments task/status counts by task and verification_state; not estimated from document class.

tiers.label: important paragraphs from substantive authorities
tiers.caution: Paragraph count and importance signals require sampled paragraph/citation/user-action data; not estimated in phase 1.

tiers.label: procedural/non-precedential material whose embedding value is uncertain
tiers.caution: Bail orders may be practically useful but are not automatically precedential. Procedural disposals are a retrieval-value experiment, not an authority tier.

tiers.label: exclude/defer
tiers.caution: The unclassified residue is model-triage work, not safe exclusion forever; reference stubs are the true hard defer in this phase.

scenarios.description: Existing dense coverage plus one document vector for TIER_A candidate authorities only.
notes: Uses sample-derived HC decided + decided_brief upper bound and all Supreme Court held rows.
Does not include unclassified DISPOSED/CLOSED residue.

scenarios.description: TIER_A plus bail-order practical material, one document vector each.
notes: Includes bail_order because criminal-practice retrieval may need it.
Still excludes DISPOSED/CLOSED residue until triaged.

scenarios.description: All plausibly useful non-procedural/non-stub material, one document vector each.
notes: Includes the unclassified DISPOSED/CLOSED residue as a triage candidate.
This is not a recommendation to embed it before classification.

scenarios.description: BALANCED plus three legal-object vectors per included document.
notes: One document vector plus three legal-object/proposition vectors per document.
Legal-object acceptance rates are not included yet; this is an upper cost envelope.
